name: openbot
description: A local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. Run Codex, Claude, and Grok with dedicated workspaces, task queues, file sharing, browser control, and agent-to-agent collaboration.
one_liner: A desktop app that gives you a small team of AI 'coworkers,' each running a different AI model, with their own workspace, a shared task queue, and the ability to message each other and hand off work.
buyer: A lean technical founder who wants to simulate having a few junior assistants to prototype internal automations, without the cost or overhead of hiring.
business_use_cases: A solo founder assigns separate AI teammates to research, drafting and QA tasks that hand off to each other via the shared task queue.
A small agency prototypes a multi-agent workflow (e.g. one agent researches, one writes, one reviews) before deciding whether to build a custom product around it.
A technical consultant demos agent-to-agent collaboration to a client as a proof-of-concept before proposing a production automation build.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a 'design your AI team' consulting engagement that configures task queues and agent roles for a specific client workflow.

steal_this: This is an explicit development preview that the authors warn runs agents with full, unconfirmed file and network access — the honest weekend move is testing it in a sandboxed VM to learn the multi-agent pattern, not deploying it for anyone's real work yet.
